method: Read the current AGENTS.md before independent review. Fully read all assigned deployment modules, tests, CI, scripts, configuration, documentation and ordinary feature evidence in bounded output ranges, rereading truncated ranges. Traced identity and root authority, immutable build and archive import, dependency preparation, request spool and receipt recovery, release/control/provider/TLS transactions, descriptor-scoped workspace operations, Git publication and worktree retention. Parsed every lock record and every capability record, checked schema/group/type bindings and all recorded file/hash references, and semantically assessed all 50 evidence groups and 15 additional workflows. Historical referenced report bodies were treated as opaque existence/SHA objects. Ran only four justified portable targeted test files. Rechecked all 115 assigned byte hashes, assignment metadata and the global frozen digest before report publication.

validations.name: Assigned coverage
validations.detail: All 115 assigned files covered; large lock and capability files received exhaustive structural record checks plus semantic review. No assigned file was skipped.

validations.name: Portable targeted tests
validations.command: node scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted tests/deploy/test_dependency_lock.py tests/deploy/test_journal_schema.py tests/deploy/test_origins.py tests/deploy/test_request_spool.py
validations.runtime: Python 3.12.14 on Windows; isolated task TEMP/TMP and bytecode disabled
validations.detail: Bounded lock reads and replacement races; current journal schema and unknown receipts; canonical origins; disconnected waiter, active executor, spool retention and replay boundaries.

validations.name: Complete dependency-lock structure
validations.detail: Consumed all 2433 nonempty lines with duplicate-key and unsupported-grammar rejection. Checked one importer against all 21 direct manifest pins; approved workspace overrides; every package integrity decodes as 64-byte SHA-512; all snapshot base packages and dependency references resolve. Inspected engine/platform/optional/peer metadata and pinned Node compatibility; no package lifecycle or network execution.

validations.name: Complete capability inventory structure and semantic assessments
validations.detail: Independently matched 178 TypeScript methods and parameter import paths, 175 JSON variants, 106 stable and 69 experimental methods, three explicit legacy methods, classifications/status counts and exact one-group ownership. All 543 path/hash references and 142 historical report references matched; supported reference line positions are in range. All 50 group and 15 workflow assessments read, including narrower filesystem/search/watch/Bedrock equivalents, authority boundaries and explicit external/platform limits.

validations.name: Ordinary evidence and opaque historical references
validations.detail: Parsed all assigned JSON and JSON-subset workspace files with duplicate-key rejection. The 99 distinct local path/hash pairs and six hashless historical artifact references exist; hashes matched wherever recorded. No referenced historical report conclusion was read or adopted as a current audit result.

validations.name: Tool and audit-helper execution errors
validations.detail: Initial PyYAML availability probe failed with ModuleNotFoundError; no package was installed. A strict local restricted-lock parser was used instead. Initial protocol regex assumed an unquoted method key; corrected to the generated quoted key. Initial parameter regex omitted two optional params fields; corrected and all 178 bindings then passed. Several large tool outputs were truncated; affected source ranges, document batches and capability method/assessment projections were reread in bounded output. These were audit-tool limitations, not product findings.

validations.name: Historical nonpassing evidence retained
validations.detail: Read existing evidence without converting it into current execution: attachments-linux records 16 passed and one Windows-only skip with runner exit 3; private-account-media records a Windows attachment run with two skips; runtime-guardian-cli-audio retains a run with two skips; linux-cli-crossuid retains seven nonpassing earlier attempts before its recorded passing attempt; provider-boundary-and-host-check retains an earlier combined probe exit 1. These evidence files remain unchanged and were not counted as newly passing tests.

validations.name: Frozen bytes before publication
validations.detail: Every assigned file matches its independently captured byte hash; assignment and snapshot metadata are unchanged. The repository snapshot command returns the assigned 1786-file digest.

limitations: This is a source audit plus 28 narrow portable tests, not full-suite or production deployment acceptance. No source fix or capability regeneration was performed.

Linux root ownership, real systemd/cgroup/mount/network-namespace behavior, reboot recovery, descriptor/Git/worktree/native subprocess paths and cross-UID fixtures were read but not executed in this Windows audit. No SSH or online instance operation occurred.
No personal credentials or homes, paid model inference, external MCP, authenticated cloud/account flows, live provider endpoints, public TLS issuance or browser identity login were exercised.

Historical feature evidence remains point-in-time evidence. Its stated failures, skips, mock boundaries and external-service limitations were retained; hash agreement proves artifact identity rather than present behavior.
Exhaustive lock structural/integrity-reference checks do not constitute downloading or executing every dependency or a fresh online vulnerability advisory query.
